messages.content: What is RAM?

RAM is your computer's short-term workspace. It holds the apps and data you are actively using so the processor can reach them quickly. More RAM helps you keep more things open, but it does not permanently store files.
Is RAM the same as storage?
No. RAM is fast, temporary workspace; storage is the longer-term place for files and apps. Turning off the computer clears RAM, while files on storage remain.
What is VRAM used for?
VRAM is memory dedicated to the graphics processor. It holds textures, frames, and other visual data so games and creative apps can draw images smoothly.
Does more VRAM always make a GPU faster?
No. More VRAM lets a GPU handle larger textures or scenes, but speed also depends on the GPU's processing cores, memory bandwidth, and the software. Extra capacity cannot fix a weak chip by itself.
What is an API?
An API is a defined way for one program to request something from another program or service. It specifies what you can ask for, what information to send, and what response to expect.
Do APIs mean two apps share all their data?
No. An API exposes only the operations and data its owner chooses. Authentication and permissions can limit which requests each person or app is allowed to make.
What does a browser do?
A browser fetches web resources, interprets HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and displays the result as a page. It also manages tabs, cookies, permissions, and security checks.
Why does clearing browser cache sometimes help?
The cache keeps local copies of web files for faster loading. If a copy is stale or damaged, deleting it makes the browser download fresh files. It may make the next load slower once.
Is a browser the same thing as a search engine?
No. A browser is the app that opens websites. A search engine is a website or service that helps you find pages; you use it through a browser.
What is the difference between an SSD and an HDD?

An SSD uses flash memory and has no moving parts, so it is usually faster and quieter. An HDD uses spinning magnetic disks and is often cheaper per terabyte, but it is slower and more sensitive to shocks.
If I delete a file, is it immediately gone?
Usually it first moves to a recycle bin or trash. Emptying that bin removes the normal reference to it, but some data may remain recoverable until storage space is reused or securely erased.
What is a computer network?
A network is a group of connected devices that exchange data. Connections can use cables, Wi-Fi, or other links, and devices follow shared rules called protocols.
What does a router do at home?
A router directs traffic between your home devices and other networks, such as your internet provider. It commonly also provides Wi-Fi, assigns local addresses, and shares one internet connection.
Why is Wi-Fi slow when I am far from the router?
Radio signals weaken with distance and can be blocked or disturbed by walls and other devices. Moving closer, reducing interference, or using an access point or cable can help.
My internet is down. Does that mean my Wi-Fi is broken?
Not necessarily. Wi-Fi is the local wireless link between your device and router; the router may still work while the provider connection is down. Check whether other devices have the same problem.
Why does restarting fix so many computer problems?
Restarting clears temporary program state, releases resources, reconnects services, and can finish updates. It does not repair every underlying fault, but it removes many short-lived glitches.
My laptop says it has 16 GB RAM, but only 15.4 GB is usable. Is it broken?
Probably not. The operating system and integrated hardware may reserve a small portion for themselves, so the usable amount is slightly lower than the installed amount.
Why do websites ask me to accept cookies?

Cookies are small pieces of site data stored by your browser. Some keep you signed in or remember preferences; others are used for measurement or advertising. The prompt asks about consent for some of those uses.
Can I put an API key in front-end JavaScript?

Assume users can see anything sent to the browser. Keep secret API keys on a server, and have the server make the protected request. A public key is different only if the service explicitly designs it to be public.
If my computer has free storage, why is it still slow?

Free storage is only one factor. Slowdowns can come from low RAM, heavy background apps, overheating, a failing drive, malware, or network delays. Check which resource is actually busy before changing hardware.
